issues.author: ClassicLarry
issues.body:
Issue is to describe the Hero Run scaling ladder, config, and track its performance.

Tracking: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng

Details on the full model spec is in the comment below.

### Why run a scaling ladder?

1. This lets us project the model performance and compare it to the scaling projections of our prior recipes. If our projection looks meaningfully worse, then we know we need to go back to the drawing board on some aspect of the model or data. This step can catch a lot of bugs!
2. We can look at how training dynamics change as we scale, in particular the gradient norms and token dropping. In our last run, the scaling ladder caught gradient norm growth to over 4 as we scaled out token horizon, which caused us to find a fix with logit z loss. Later ablations showed that without this fix, runs under certain conditions like high batch size would completely blow up mid-run.
3. We can project our evals across the entire trajectory of the run. This means that across the entire ~100 day run, we know exactly how we are doing compared to the projection. If at any point we fail to match the projection, it can prompt early investigation into training dynamics.
4. If something strange start to happen in the Hero run, we can reference the smaller scales runs to see if its actually normal. For instance, in prior scaling ladders we saw the grad norm grow heavily up to 40% of the run, then decrease as the LR decays. When we saw this on the hero run, having the small scale reference gave us confidence we didn't need to intervene, as long as the gradient followed the same pattern (steady growth for 40% of run).
5. It only costs 1% of total compute.
### What is our EP hardware implementation?
Described in detail here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html.
We are hand-rolling our own EP implementation, props to @ravwojdyla, since we have not found a more performant variant on JAX XLA on GPU. 

### What is our long context extension plan?
Our last run was 8k seqlen pretrain, followed by 65k extension for 1T tokens, followed by 262k extension (to occur end of Aug). Prior to that run we have used 4k seqlen pretrain. For this run we are going back to 4k seqlen pretrain to start, to enable better expert balancing (twice as many sequences per batch). We wanted to minimize risk here because our EP token dropping implementation is more experimental. (our last run was dropless FSDP). Prior tests showed token dropping grow from ~7% to ~40% when extending from 4k to 65k seqlen. Our new pooled/wave EP drops about half as many tokens (3%) at 4k seqlen; however the token dropping is likely still excessively high at 65k seqlen.

We will spend 1-2 days to do an early cooldown at roughly 10-20 days into the run, to enable RL experiments, which will be our first full scale data point at how longer context influences dropping. A nice property of this test is that the cooldown will not contaminate or impact the main run, so we have some flexibility to collect data on how an extension approach impacts dropping. Our options will be:
1. If we have landed a Jax Mixture of Kittens or dropless ragged all-to-all, then we can swap to that for the cooldown. Prior small scale tests showed the model was robust from swapping from small amounts of dropping (5%) to dropless mid-run.
2. Otherwise, we can increase our capacity factor, and accept some amount of dropping.
3. If we find that neither of these options are suitable, the next option would be to introduce sequence level balancing mid-run (though forcing the experts to re-specialize mid-run will likely be worse than accepting some amount of dropping). 

Extending context will involve updating qk_mult according to mscale=X⋅ln(new_seqlen/old_seqlen)+1, testing coefficients near 0.1 (can quickly eval a range during extension on 1 rack). If the data from the first cooldown looks smooth, will plan on 4k->8k at 50 pct into run, then 8k->65k at about 95 pct, then a targeted 262k phase near end, based on data we collect from taking the 67B-A2B from 65k to 262k.

Have further derisked token dropping by staying at 2 shared experts, each at half width. 8 active experts are also at half width. However due to latent MoE 2x compression on active experts, we are effectively running at hidden_dim width neurons shared, and 2x hidden_dim neurons routed. Having 1/3 of our neurons come from shared expert will provide a stronger backbone in the event of high dropping. We see learning still progress with zero loss spikes even at 40 pct dropping.

### What if we see delays, beyond our buffer (hardware failure, MFU degradation)?
Up to roughly 25% of the token budget, the default approach will be to compensate by decreasing the token horizon of the run. Since we are using linear LR decay, we would update the decay rate to still reach 0.05 peak at whatever the new horizon point is, and update the datamix.

🤖 # Job Summary: Aug Hero Run — 535B-A23B MoE (d6144), 18T tokens

Full-scale EP64 MoE pretrain: d6144, **535.3B total / 22.76B active** params, **18.0T tokens** (~**2.70e24** train FLOPs, fwd+bwd), on GB200 with our hand-rolled pooled-wave expert-parallel all-to-all. Data is the two-phase Harrier mixture on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store. Below: model, optimizer, training/topology, the MFU optimizations, the scaling ladder, and outputs.

## 1. Model

### Hyperparameters
| | |
|---|---|
| hidden_dim | 6144 |
| num_layers | 48 |
| num_heads | 48 · head_dim 128 |
| num_kv_heads | 12 stored — **local 12 / global 6** (GQA 4:1 local, 8:1 global) |
| num_experts / top-k | **384 / 8** |
| intermediate_dim (expert FFN) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |
| latent_dim (LatentMoE) | 3072 (= hidden/2) |
| shared experts | 2 dense SwiGLU, width 3072 |
| vocab_size | 128,256 |
| max_seq_len | 4096 · sliding_window 2048 · global_every 4 |
| capacity_factor / transport cf | 1.15 / 1.15 · num_expert_waves 3 |
| qk_mult | 1.3 · rope θ=10000 (fused, half-RoPE) |
| sconv | sites k/attn/mlp, kernel 4 |
| init | 0.5/√hidden = 0.006379 (uniform, truncated normal) |
| active / total params | 22.76B / 535.3B |

### Features
All structural (always on) unless noted.
- **All-MoE**: every block's MLP is a QB-routed `MoEMLP`; no dense-only layers.
- **GQA, split local/global KV**: sliding-window (local) layers keep 12 KV heads, full-causal (global) layers 6; K/V are sliced/aligned per layer via `lax.cond`, so global layers pay less KV compute.
- **QB routing (histogram estimator)**: router takes top-(K+1) on biased logits; the (K+1)-th logit is the per-token threshold `alpha`, the first K are selected. Each expert's threshold `beta` is the **(1−K/E) upper quantile of the margins `score−alpha`**, read from a **10k-bin histogram over the live global `[min, max]` range** (a `pmin`/`pmax` this step sets the grid; a summed-histogram cumulative count gives the per-expert quantile). The router bias `−beta` is applied on the **next step** as a zero-mean stop-gradient offset — balances expert selection without touching gradients. The histogram estimator is a smoother global quantile than a per-device top-k.
- **Sigmoid combine weights**: combine weights are `sigmoid(unbiased selected logits)`, rescaled so the K weights sum to a fixed 2.5 (not softmax).
- **LatentMoE + learnable latent RMS-norm**: tokens are compressed `hidden→latent (3072)`, passed through a **learnable RMSNorm (`latent_norm`, per-dim gain)** to decouple the expert-input scale from the down-projection init, then dispatched to experts **entirely in latent space**, and projected `latent→hidden` after the weighted combine. The router still reads the full-width token. (Also halves the all-to-all payload — see §4.)
- **Shared experts**: 2 dense SwiGLU experts run on every token in parallel with the routed path; their output is added before the residual.
- **RMSNorm on embeddings and readout**: a learnable-gain [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594) is applied to the token embeddings ([`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223)) and before the untied `lm_head` ([`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1165)), in addition to the per-block `rms_attn`/`rms_mlp`; the GatedNorm below wraps each of these.
- **GatedNorm**: learnable `x·sigmoid(silu(x·w_down)·w_up)` gate (rank-128 bottleneck) applied after **every** RMSNorm (attn, mlp, embed, final).
- **XSA (Exclusive Self-Attention)**: per head, subtract the component of the attention output parallel to its own value vector: `z = y − (yᵀv/‖v‖²)v` — removes the copy-through component so each head learns new information rather than passing V unchanged.
- **Attention head gate**: each head's attention output is scaled by a learned `2·sigmoid(x·attn_gate)`, one scalar per head; `attn_gate` is zero-initialized (gate starts at 1).
- **RMS qk-norm**: Q and K are RMS-normed (non-parametric) per head before RoPE.
- **Partial (half) RoPE, fused**: rotary is applied to **only the first half of head_dim**; the second half is rope-free on every layer. Single-pass fused kernel (θ=10000).
- **Rope-free global layers**: every 4th layer + the last are full-causal and **rope-free** (NoPE, qk_mult-only); the others are sliding-window with RoPE. One per-layer boolean drives mask, KV-head count, and rope together.
- **ShortConv (SConv)**: depthwise causal 1-D conv (kernel 4), identity-init, packed-document segment-masked, at three sites — after K, on the attention-branch output, on the MoE-branch output.
- **Embeddings**: `token_embed` fully replicated + shard-local lookup; `lm_head` (`output_proj`) FSDP+model-sharded; **untied**.
- **Logit z-loss**: the final-logit logsumexp is penalized (`logsumexp_weight = z_loss_weight = 1e-4`) and **added to the training loss** (fused into the CE) — controls gradient-norm growth at long token horizons (the fix the prior scaling ladder surfaced). Distinct from the router z-loss, which is logging-only.
- **Monitoring** (logged, not in loss): per-layer routing entropy, load-balance loss, router z-loss, and sender/receiver token-drop fractions.

## 2. Optimizer — MuonH / AdamH / Adam (compute-scaled)

Three groups via `optax.multi_transform` + a path mask:
- **MuonH** — attention, expert-MLP, shared-expert, latent, and GatedNorm **matrices**. Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (bf16, `backend_steps=5`, quintic coeffs, nesterov momentum 0.95) → **Frobenius-hyperball** scale-invariant step (moves along the direction, projects back onto the param's Frobenius sphere; norms in fp32). Orthogonalization is distributed **intra-rack only** (never crosses DCN); 4D expert stacks are handled without gathering the matrix dims.
- **AdamH** — the **lm_head readout**: Adam moments give the direction, then the same norm-preserving hyperball projection. Gets the MuonH LR, not `adam_lr`.
- **Adam** — `token_embed`, router, router_bias, `attn_gate`, 1-D norm gains, and the tiny SConv kernels.

### Hyperparameters (@ 18T budget)
| | |
|---|---|
| MuonH LR | 0.003291 |
| Adam LR | 0.000759 (MuonH = 13/3 × Adam = 4.33×) |
| beta1 / beta2 | **0.90** / 0.95 |
| epsilon | 6.04e-15 (Adam) · muon_epsilon 1e-8 |
| momentum / nesterov | 0.95 / true |
| use_syrk | true (Blackwell SM100 symmetric GEMM for X·Xᵀ) |
| LR schedule | linear · warmup 1% · min_lr_ratio 0.05 |
| max_grad_norm | none (no global clip) |
| z_loss_weight | 1e-4 (logit z-loss, fused into CE) |

The MuonH/AdamH groups carry **no decoupled weight decay** — they regularize purely through the norm-preserving hyperball projection. LR / beta2 / epsilon are compute-scaled from the Aug hero refit (issues #7856 / #8003, R²=0.978, seq_len=8192): `adam_lr = 0.087571 · tokens^-0.3461 · hidden^-0.3448 · √(tokens_per_batch)`, `beta2 = clip(0.999^(tpb/131072), 0.95, 0.9999)`, `epsilon = 9.676e-18 · √(tokens/tpb)`.

## 3. Training & topology
- **Hardware**: 11× GB200 NVL72 racks. **EP64 within each rack** (expert axis = 16 nodes × 4 GPUs), **data-parallel replication across the 11 racks over DCN**. Mesh `(replica_dcn=11, data, expert=64, model)`; token/batch sharded over `(replica_dcn, data, expert)`.
- **batch_size** 11,264 seqs (1024 × 11 racks) · **seq_len** 4096 · **num_train_steps** 390,139 · **total_tokens 18.0T** · **791 tokens/active-param**.
- **compute_budget** ≈ 2.70e24 FLOPs (analytic, fwd+bwd, latent-corrected).
- **mixed_precision** `params=bf16, compute=bf16, output=bf16`, with **fp32 pinned-host master params** + **offloaded optimizer state** (see §4). Router path kept fp32 before top-k/softmax/QB stats.
- **data**: two-phase Harrier mixture (15T pretrain + 3.75T cooldown, phase-1 at 80% of steps) on the fuzzy-deduped datakit store, marin tokenizer; simulated epoching against the 18.75T reference with a ≤8-epoch cap (max cell exposure ~2.1). 4k-seq pretrain deliberately (2× sequences/batch for expert balancing; token-drop grows sharply at longer context).

## 4. MFU / performance optimizations
- **Hand-rolled fixed pooled-wave all-to-all EP** — every device packs sends into one fixed `[expert_shards, pool_capacity]` pool and receives into fixed per-wave `[local_experts, receiver_cap, H]` buffers; all sizes are compile-time constants so the `all_to_all` runs on fully static shapes. Chosen over `ragged_all_to_all` to avoid a metadata/offset collective and dynamic shapes; **expert IDs ride in-band** as packed header rows in the same activation collective (no separate metadata collective). [EP writeup](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/moe-fixed-wave-a2a-384/2026.08.17/index.html)
- **Static waves (3)** stripe each destination pool round-robin by rank, shrinking per-wave buffers; each wave is rematerialized to cap activation memory. **Round-robin receiver allocation** keeps overflow drops unbiased across senders.
- **LatentMoE halves EP transport bytes** — the all-to-all carries latent-width (3072) rows both directions instead of hidden (6144). FLOP accounting is corrected for this so MFU isn't overstated.
- **gpu_fa4_cute FA4 attention** — bf16 CuTe segmented flash attention with per-token key lower bounds (no materialized `[B,S,S]` mask, no THD compaction), real GQA, custom CUTLASS backward, grug-tuned 64×64 tiles for B200/head_dim-128. **Sliding-window vs full-causal is just a different lower-bound array feeding the same kernel** → cuts attention FLOPs on the ~3/4 local layers. Bounds are precomputed **outside** the layer scan.
- **Fused linear-softmax cross-entropy (bf16 backward)** — `implementation="xla_fast_bwd"`: streams the whole 65,536-token rank shard over `v_block=4096` vocab blocks with online logsumexp (never materializes the `[B,128k]` logits), and runs both **backward GEMMs in bf16 on tensor cores** (vs fp32/TF32) for ~2.3× on the hero CE shape; the logit z-loss is fused as `logsumexp_weight·lse²`. `v_block=4096` is the dominant MFU lever for the 128k vocab.
- **Fused depthwise causal ShortConv (Pallas)** — the SConv sites dispatch to a fused **Pallas Triton depthwise causal conv** kernel on GPU (forward and `dx` bit-identical to the pad-and-shift reference, `dw` as accurate; pad-and-shift fallback off-GPU). Shard-local (depthwise, no cross-channel/cross-shard term → no collectives); the channel dim is FSDP-sharded so its gradient reduce-scatters.
- **Muon symmetric-GEMM (QuACK SM100) Newton–Schulz** — the two `X·Xᵀ` products in each Newton–Schulz iteration go through a **QuACK symmetric CuTe GEMM** (`use_syrk`) that computes only one triangle of the symmetric output (`A = X·Xᵀ`, then `B = b·A + c·(A·Aᵀ)`) instead of a full dense matmul — roughly halves the matmul FLOPs per iteration on the batched 4D expert stacks, where orthogonalization is the bulk of the optimizer's compute.
- **Padded + resharded distributed Muon (intra-rack)** — the stacked leaves are orthogonalized in parallel across the rack instead of gathered to one device: 3D non-expert stacks **zero-pad the leading (layer) axis** so it divides the intra-rack shard count, then reshard the padded stack over the batch mesh axes (one matrix per shard, `vmap`'d, resliced back after); 4D expert stacks `[layers, experts, fan_in, fan_out]` reshard over the `expert` axis (or the largest batch-axis subset that divides `layers·experts`) and run under a `shard_map` **without ever gathering the `fan_in×fan_out` matrix dims**, then reshard back to the parameter's own spec. All of this is pinned **intra-rack only** — the reshards deliberately exclude the `replica_dcn` axis so Newton–Schulz never runs a collective over the slow inter-rack DCN link.
- **ArrayStacked + `jax.lax.scan`** — all 48 blocks are one compiled body scanned over the layer axis, cutting compile time and HBM; router/QB collectives are structured around the scan.
- **Heterogeneous global/local layers under one homogeneous scan** — `lax.scan` needs a single compiled body, so the ways global (full-causal, rope-free) and local (sliding-window) layers differ can't be Python branches — each rides in as a traced per-layer scalar and is selected *inside* the body:
  - **RoPE diff** — global layers run rope-free. Rather than branch, RoPE is **always computed** and then selected with `jnp.where` on a per-layer `disable_rope` scalar, so both layer kinds compile to the same body.
  - **GQA diff** — local layers keep 12 KV heads, global layers 6. K/V are stored at the max (12) width and sliced-then-`align_kv_heads`'d to the per-layer count via `lax.cond(is_global, …)`, so global layers pay less KV compute without changing the stacked parameter shape.
  - **Mask diff** — the full-causal and sliding-window FA4 bound arrays are precomputed **outside** the scan and the per-layer one is picked with `jnp.where` (the sliding window is a static mask field the body can't vary), so the window rides in as the selected bounds.
- **remat `recompute_all`** — the whole block is recomputed in backward (lowest memory); a `save_moe` mode is available to keep the MoE dispatch tensors and skip re-running the EP collectives.
- **Capacity-factor token dropping (1.15)** bounds expert compute and transport buffers regardless of routing imbalance; drops are counted/logged as sender/receiver fractions.
- **use_syrk** routes the optimizer's `X·Xᵀ` through QuACK's SM100 symmetric GEMM; Newton–Schulz runs in bf16 (halved all-gather bytes) and **intra-rack only**.
- **offload_opt_state + FP32_PINNED_HOST master** — optimizer state and fp32 master weights live in pinned host RAM, shuttled device↔host each step, to leave HBM for the pooled all-to-all buffers. (The pinned-host restore is fixed in [#8443](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8443) and memory-bounded in [#8480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8480); the hero now writes an hourly temporary checkpoint and resumes from it after a preemption.)
- **XLA/runtime flags** — latency-hiding scheduler on, collective-overlap limit 4, CUDA async allocator, 192GB host-memory limit, PGLE off, GPU command buffers disabled.

## 5. Scaling ladder (why, and the rungs)
Runs at 5 widths on one iso-ratio recipe (**791 tokens/active-param**, same mixture + simulated epoching + per-cell epoch structure), ≈1% of total compute, to (a) project performance vs prior recipes and catch bugs, (b) watch grad-norm and token-drop dynamics across scale (the last ladder caught grad-norm growth → the logit z-loss fix), and (c) project evals across the ~100-day trajectory.

| rung | racks | batch | steps | tokens | active |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d768 | 1 | 1024 | 11,420 | 48B | 61M |
| d1024 | 2 | 2048 | 15,276 | 128B | 162M |
| d1536 | 6 | 6144 | 15,128 | 381B | 481M |
| d2048 | 11 | 11,264 | 20,072 | 926B | 1.2B |
| **d6144 (hero)** | 11 | 11,264 | 390,139 | **18.0T** | 22.8B |

## 6. Code (at run commit [`12d8b6f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be))

**Model** ([`model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py)) — [`GrugModelConfig`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L160)
- All-MoE routed FFN: [`MoEMLP`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L907) · shared experts [`DenseMLP`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L637)
- QB routing (histogram estimator): threshold/beta [`_qb_beta_hist`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L874), histogram build [`_histogram_from_expert_counts`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L820), applied next-step as stop-grad bias
- Sigmoid combine + renorm-to-2.5: [`_ROUTING_RENORM_SUM`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L58), [combine](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L980)
- LatentMoE + learnable latent RMSNorm: [`latent_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1046)
- RMSNorm on embeddings/readout: [`embed_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1223), [`final_norm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1203); [`RMSNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L594)
- GatedNorm: [`GatedNorm`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L612)
- XSA (exclusive self-attention): [subtract V-parallel component](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L573)
- Attention head gate (zero-init): [`attn_gate`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L583)
- RMS qk-norm: [`rms_norm(q)`,`rms_norm(k)`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L534)
- Partial (half) RoPE, fused: [`_rope`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L553), [`rope_fused`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L541); rope-free global layers via per-layer bounds [L1252](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1252)
- ShortConv: [`ShortConv`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L420) → fused Pallas [`short_conv`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L52)
- Attention (FA4-cute): [call](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L572), [`fa4_cute_segment_bounds`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1252)
- Untied embeddings: [`token_embed`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1160), [`output_proj`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1163)
- Homogeneous global/local scan (rope diff + GQA diff): [`ArrayStacked` scan body](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1262), rope-free select via [`jnp.where(disable_rope)`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L568), per-layer KV-head [`lax.cond(is_global)`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L521), per-layer mask-bounds [select](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1268)

**Optimizer** — MuonH/AdamH/Adam
- Group mask (which param → which group): [`create_mask`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/12d8b6f09f96ad4f0277445765c1a00dbc81d5be/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/optimizer.py#L195)

comments.author: Helw150
comments.body:
## Raw Data

On the raw data side, our pool for this hero run is logged at this frozen commit of [our data provenance table on hugging face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/token-counts/commit/3612ddc3350212e38ce8a50b99c3df7ea10b44a9). The raw (pre-dedupe) pool contains 25.6 trillion tokens from 292 sources (though >100 of those are a variety of rollout datasets courtesy of @penfever!).

## Deduplication & Decontamination

For this run, we removed 2.494T tokens through a combination of  fuzzy deduplication and n-gram based decontamination w.r.t many common benchmarks in LM-eval-harness + the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (~250k documents were removed) for a final count of 23.106T tokens. 

Fuzzy duplication used a combination of MinHash deduplication and heuristics among linked pairs within connected component clusters. Examples of duplicates can be found here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/dedup-pair-browser/2026.08.18.2/index.html

## Bucketing

We then embedded all documents with [Harrier 0.6b](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/harrier-oss-v1-0.6b). 

For topic labels, documents were grouped into 40 semantic buckets by first performing K-means with 5000 clusters (using a sample of 2.56 Million documents) and then doing agglomerative clustering over those 500 clusters to get 40 buckets.

For quality labels, documents were labeled using GLM 5.2 for quality and these labels were distilled into a "Faster Transformer" classifier using both the harrier embedding and the token distribution of the document.

You can see samples from each bucket + distributions from source -> topic x document buckets here: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/harrier-k40-cluster-overview/2026.08.18/index.html?revision=uniform-sampling

🤖 Scaling-ladder analysis for the **535B-A23B, 18T-token** hero. The ladder trains one uniform hero EP recipe at five widths; four rungs finished and the d2048 rung crashed at ~81%. Fitting a power law across the rungs (`L = 1.5 + A·C^-α`, compute excludes lm_head) and extrapolating to the hero's compute predicts a final **dropless paloma macro-loss ≈ 2.04**.

**Hero prediction by training percentile** — the four measured rungs plus the d6144 hero prediction at every 5% (dashed/hollow = extrapolated).
![hero prediction by percentile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/d23e6e9c3673435fb82d83aa6c51a607d0da6009/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/scaling_ladder_figs/hero_prediction_by_percentile.png)

**Per-5% scaling-law fits (log-log)** — one power-law fit per training fraction; the crimson points trace the hero prediction out to hero-scale compute, ending at 2.039 @100%.

**Method check** — a linear extrapolation from each finished rung's 60–80% window predicts its own 100% dropless macro-loss to within ~0.003–0.004 (consistently a hair optimistic, since the curve flattens under cosine decay).
![60-80 extrapolation vs actual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/d23e6e9c3673435fb82d83aa6c51a607d0da6009/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/scaling_ladder_figs/ladder_extrapolation_60_80.png)

**Full-granularity training cross-entropy** — every step, with the datamix phase-2 boundary at 80% (a small loss bump is visible in every rung at that point).
![training cross-entropy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/d23e6e9c3673435fb82d83aa6c51a607d0da6009/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/scaling_ladder_figs/ladder_train_ce_fullres.png)

Prior precedent for this kind of extrapolation — the 67B-A2B 10T run's preregistered (80%) and two retroactive (21%, 63%) scaling-law fits each predicted that run's target within ~0.6% (issue #6044):
![67B scaling fits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/d23e6e9c3673435fb82d83aa6c51a607d0da6009/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/scaling_ladder_figs/scaling_fit_67b_prereg_vs_retro.png)

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: Comparing our scaling law to prior runs. The main differences here is that the May recipe is at compute optimal, this run is at ~12x overtrained, and the 67B-A2B scaling law was at 100x overtrained. The 67B-A2B ran at 8k seqlen, and was therefore given a lower asympotote of 1.4 instead of 1.5. The May fit also inaccurately has an asympotote at 1.6 instead of 1.5. Main architecture change is we dropped from 4/256 level of sparsity to 4/192 level of sparsity (25% fewer total parameters, to fit on GB200 at this scale. Several other small features added. Overall, the scaling law looks reasonable and nothing looks off in the training dynamics or data. Grad norms look stable over the run, peaking at 25% into the run. These runs ran at oversized batch sizes, which may be slightly suppressing the gradient. Expecting the grad norm to climb higher on the hero run, but still peak at the same ~25% into the run. This will be good metric to monitor for issues. Drop rate jumps to 10 pct at very start, then drops to 0, then climbs to ~4pct over the run. Slightly increasing as we scale. Predicting we wont have that 10 percent spike for the hero, because our warmup (1 percent) will cover a much larger number of steps since the hero is at a higher step count. I think most likely scenario is the hero runs around 2 percent dropping, but up to 8 percent seems plausible bsaed on the data at 4k seqlen.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body: Also noting- the d2048 scaling ladder rung failed at 81%. Chose not to resume to add more time to Hero Run. The dynamics look clear from the first 81 percent, and we can cleanly extrapolate the last 19%. From a practical perspective, we will not actually be running the end of the run at 4k seqlen, and the datamix may update midrun. So the utility of the scaling law is more around the first 50 percent of the run and ensuring the projection is reasonably within expectation (which it is).

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
From model perspective, main risk points during the run:

1. First 3%. Can we get through LR warmup and reach steady dynamics? If we see gradient run away/large issues here, we likely need to revisit initialization, or potentially initial batch size. Or increase capacity factor if the issue involves high dropping.
2. 30% mark. Gradient may peak, and we will see if gradient keeps climbing, or if its starts to cooldown. Indication that it keeps climbing indefinitely could indicate we need stronger logit z loss, lower token dropping, or revisit some of the norm constraints.
3. Context Extension. How will token dropping respond? See initial Issue desc.
4. Very low loss regime. If training plateaus or acts strange near end of run only, first things to check will be the numerics.

Health checklist:

1. Is total grad norm oscillating steadily? In our May 16B active run, the grad norm grew steadily to 1.5 and training was still very smooth. So I am less concerned with the absolute magnitude, and more concerned with the rate of change. Hyperball makes comparing absolute magnitude not apples to apples with AdamW runs.
2. Are all Hyberball constrained parameters actually respecting the constraint? In past we have seen bug where JAX does norm calculation incorrectly, due to some transient sharding issue. This has been updated to a more explicit calculation that seemed to resolve that issue, but issues of a similar nature may arise.
3. Is token dropping following similar trend as scaling ladder?
4. Is loss decreasing steadily?
5. Are evals decreasing steadily?
6. Is our router bias terms behaving steadily?
7. Does router entropy stay near max?
8. Is embed norm growth reasonable?
9. Is MFU holding constant?
10. Is LR schedule (both Adam and MuonH params) actually following the correct schedule?
11. Does the entire wandb config look accurate?
12. Are we hitting the projected eval targets at each 5 percent?

## Description

Identify some reasonable midtraining and/or mixes and get them downloaded/processed into Marin. Main criteria is that we want to see meaningful performance differences on some benchmarks (e.g., MATH, Humaneval) at an ~8b scale (w.r.t. the capabilities of the Marin Delphi/Isoflops ladders) from training on these mixes. We should start with benchmarks that are easy enough to see differences at this scale; we can later move on to harder benchmarks (e.g., AIME, SWE-bench, Terminal Bench).

### Definition of done

Document the mixes in this issue and/or link to another issue that already did something similar. Should have a file (e.g., `experiments/midtraining_data.py` that has pointers to Executor steps for all the mixes (similar to `experiments/models.py`).

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **Update — kicking off the midtraining recipe candidates with `nemotron-cc-math` (4plus tier)**

Picked **`nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus`** as the first dataset to anchor on: it's the Phi-4-cleaned, top-quality band of Nemotron-CC-Math (no Qwen-generated text), already tokenized at `gs://marin-us-central2/...` (~52 B llama3 tokens), so we can run pure-math sweeps without any new ingestion. Mix registry now lives at `experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`:

- `full_highquality_nemo_math` — 100 % `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus`
- `33p_67m_highquality_nemo_math` — 33 % Nemotron pretrain replay (`nemotron_mix`) + 67 % `4plus`
- `67p_33m_highquality_nemo_math` — 67 % replay + 33 % `4plus` (Mantis-style ratio)

The harness for the sweeps is `experiments/exp_delphi_math_10b_midtrain.py`. Bases are the AdamH compute-optimal Delphi/Isoflops checkpoints; every run loads weights only (`MODEL_ONLY`) with fresh AdamH momentum, 500-step warmup → linear decay, `min_lr_ratio=0.1`, `peak_lr` swept at `{0.5, 0.67, 0.83} × pretrain peak`.

**Bases:** 1e20 stand-in = `isoflop-3e+20-d2048-L21-B128` (1.9 B); 1e21 = `…-1e+21-v5-019021` (3.4 B); 1e22 = `…-1e+22-v5-025b0e` (9.7 B).

W&B project: [`marin-community/delphi-midtraining`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/delphi-midtraining).

---

comments.body:
🤖 **Update — principled 36-cell sweep across 3 scales (K=0.20 of pretrain budget per cell)**  *(edited 2026-05-06: 1e21 finished, intermediate-HF cadence corrected)*

Building on the earlier ad-hoc 9-cell pure-math + 12-cell mixture grids in the previous comment, we ran a single principled **3 mix × 4 LR × 3 scale = 36-cell sweep** that varies one knob per axis and holds everything else fixed.

**Axes:**
- **Mix** (3): `p33m67`, **`p50m50`** (new), `p67m33` — pretrain-replay : `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus` ratio.
- **LR factor** (4): 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, **0.83** — multiplier on each base's pretrain peak LR. We extended the prior `{0.5, 0.67, 0.83}` set down to 0.33 because the prior comment's "LR barely matters" claim only held at the high end.
- **Scale** (3): 1e20, 1e21, 1e22 base pretrain FLOPs.

**Key methodology change** vs the prior comment: each cell midtrains for a **fixed fraction `K = 0.20` of its base's pretrain token budget**, not a fixed 10 B / 20 B. So `step / final_step` is directly comparable across scales, which lets us cleanly ask whether a cheap 1e20 sweep transfers to 1e22:

| Scale | Pretrain tokens | Midtrain tokens (`K=0.20`) | Steps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1e20 | 24.67 B | 4.94 B | 9 413 |
| 1e21 | 46.27 B | 9.25 B | 4 411 |
| 1e22 | 160.37 B | 32.07 B | 7 647 |

**Held fixed across cells:** bases are the AdamH compute-optimal Delphi v5 checkpoints (`adamh-scaling-ladder-nemotron-optimal-{1e+20,1e+21,1e+22}-v5-...`); weights-only resume with fresh AdamH momentum; 500-step warmup → linear decay to `min_lr_ratio=0.1`; Llama-3.1 tokenizer; `seq_len=4096`. Sweep harness: `experiments/exp_delphi_math_10b_midtrain.py`.

**Hardware footprint per cell** (wall-clock incl. any preemption/resume):
- 1e20 → **~7.5 h on v5p-32**
- 1e21 → **~10 h on v5p-64** (or ~4.5 h on v5p-128)
- 1e22 → **~20 h on v5p-256**

### Logging — what's available beyond train loss

- **W&B project**: [`marin-community/delphi-midtraining`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/delphi-midtraining).
- **Held-out math validation set**: `eval/nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus/loss` — **12 500 sequences ≈ 51.2 M tokens** held out from `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus` via a deterministic Feistel index split (`DEFAULT_VAL_SEQUENCES_PER_MIDTRAIN_COMPONENT` in `experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`). The model never sees these during midtraining, the same sequences are held out at every scale, and final-loss SE is well below 0.001 — so cross-scale validation losses are directly comparable. Eval cadence every 200 train steps.
- **Pretrain-retention validation**: `eval/paloma/macro_loss` (Paloma macro) and `eval/paloma/c4_en/loss` (Paloma C4-en) — directly measure how much midtraining shifts the model away from the pretrain distribution.
- **Aggregate**: `eval/loss` (default eval set), useful but blends math gain and retention damage.
- **Intermediate Levanter checkpoints**: `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/{run_name}/checkpoints/step-{step}/`.
- **Intermediate HF checkpoints**: `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/{run_name}/hf/step-{step}/` — Levanter exports HF at every permanent-checkpoint cadence, **not** only at the final step. Each cell has ~10 intermediate HF snapshots across the run: every 941 steps for 1e20 (10 snapshots `step-941, …, step-9410, step-9412`), every 441 steps for 1e21, every 764 steps for 1e22. Use these to study midtraining dynamics, eval intermediate states, or fine-tune from a partial.

### Findings (per-cell endpoints, finished cells only)

1. **Recipe ranks generalize cleanly across scales.** For all three objectives, the top recipe at 1e20 is also the top recipe at 1e21 and 1e22.
   - **Math objective**: `p33m67` mix dominates at every scale. Within `p33m67`, `lr=0.83` narrowly wins at 1e20 (+0.6783 vs +0.6765 for `lr=0.67`); `lr=0.67` wins at 1e21 (+0.6731) and 1e22 (+0.7058). Practical pick across all scales: `p33m67` with `lr ∈ {0.67, 0.83}`.
   - **Paloma retention**: `p67m33-lr=0.33` is least damaging at every scale (actually retention-*positive*: −0.027 to −0.019).
   - **Aggregate `eval/loss`**: top-2 cells are `p33m67-lr=0.33` and `p33m67-lr=0.5` at every scale. Optimal LR drifts down with scale (`lr=0.5` at 1e20 → `lr=0.33` at 1e21/1e22), but the cross-LR gap is ~0.0007 — within run-to-run noise.

2. **LR matters once you care about retention.** The prior comment's "LR factor barely matters" claim held only at the {0.5, 0.67, 0.83} end. Adding `lr=0.33` shows the math-Paloma trade-off is monotone in LR within each mix.

3. **Paloma damage compounds with scale.** At fixed `p33m67-lr=0.5`, damage goes +0.028 → +0.033 → +0.045 across 1e20 → 1e21 → 1e22 (~60 % larger retention tax at 1e22).

4. **Math improvement does compound at 1e22.** The prior "math gains don't compound with scale" line held only between 1e20 and 1e21 (Δ ≤ 0.003). The 1e21 → 1e22 jump adds +0.03 to +0.04 at every fixed (mix, LR).

5. **Mix-gap (`p33m67 − p67m33` on math) is stable at ~0.10** across all three scales (1e20: 0.103, 1e21: 0.106, 1e22: 0.106 at lr=0.5) — the math advantage of math-heavy mixes is approximately scale-invariant.

6. **`p50m50` (new) sits between the other two mixes** on every metric and at every scale. Never strictly best except as a low-LR Paloma-aware compromise.

**Practical takeaway**: sweeping at 1e20 and trusting the choice transfers to 1e22 is justified for the math/Paloma trade. Expect a small downward LR drift at larger scales for retention-aware objectives, but no rank changes.

### Status — **33 of 36 cells with usable HF final checkpoint**

- 1e20: **12/12 ✅**
- 1e21: **12/12 ✅** (both previously-in-progress cells `p33m67 lr0.83` and `p67m33 lr0.67`-resume completed since the original comment)
- 1e22: **9/12 ✅** + 3 partial (Levanter checkpoints preserved, no final HF yet): `p33m67 lr0.83`, `p50m50 lr0.5`, `p50m50 lr0.67`.

Inference-quick-start, Qwen3-vs-LlamaForCausalLM config-bug workaround, and `rope_scaling` repair recipe are documented in `.agents/handoffs/delphi-midtrain-finished-runs.md` in the worktree.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **Correction to prior Delphi midtraining updates: the `1e20` rows were not trained from a Delphi base.**

Discovered on 2026-05-14: every result previously reported here under the `1e20` label used

```text
isoflop-3e+20-d2048-L21-B128-adamh_scaling_v5
```

as its base checkpoint. That is a deprecated v5 isoflop ablation point, not the canonical Delphi/v6 scaling-law bucket winner.

The closest canonical sub-1e21 Delphi-family anchor is:

```text
isoflop-3e+20-d2304-L23-B128-adamh_scaling_v6
```

There is no `1e20 Delphi` model. Delphi proper starts at `1e21`; the `3e20` v6 isoflop winner is one of the bucket points used to fit the scaling law.

What this changes:

- The `1e20` HF checkpoints in earlier comments are still valid trained artifacts, but should be labeled `v5-isoflop-3e20` / non-Delphi, not `Delphi 1e20`.
- Claims that rely on `1e20 -> 1e22` transfer are weakened because the `1e20` point is from a different scaling family.
- The `1e21 -> 1e22` comparisons still stand as within-family Delphi evidence.
- The apparent mix-gap stability across `1e20/1e21/1e22` should be read as `1e21/1e22` stability plus a contaminated/non-family `1e20` reference point.

Local follow-up is tracked in `.agents/ops/2026-05-14-wrong-1e20-base-v5-vs-v6.md`. Going forward, Delphi base selection should come from `experiments/delphi_models.py`; do not pick base checkpoints by grepping GCS paths.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **Nemotron math val-set contamination: findings + clean-val plan**

We investigated whether the math val carve-out (12,500 windows, 51.2M tokens, 57,243 docs from `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus`) is contaminated by train near-duplicates. tl;dr: heavily, and it scales with isoflop budget; we are rebuilding a clean doc-level val set.

**Exact dup**: zero (45.1M xxh3_128 ids unique). Stochastic extraction means near-dups never hash equal — same page reappears with different whitespace/heading levels (J 0.75-1.0 examples verified by hand).

**Fuzzy contamination (initial 286/26 LSH, ~67% recall @ J0.75)**: 17% of val docs / 18.6% of val tokens had a J>=0.75 dup in train; 54.7% of windows touched.

**Per-scale exposure** (replayed sampling; combined J>=0.75 + same-doc): 3e18 ~1.2% of val tokens -> 1e22 39.4%. The 1e22 "too good" math val loss is memorization headroom, not data efficiency.

**High-recall rescans (284 perms / 71 bands, ~99% recall @ J0.5)** across the math family:
- 4plus: 32,619 val docs with J>=0.5 dup (old banding found 20,850 — undercounted 56%)
- 3: 13,238 cross-subset
- 4plus_mind: running (synthetic MIND rewrites of 4plus pages — expect heavy overlap; 193 GB of LSH candidates vs 93 GB for 4plus)

**Doc-level dedupe (drop doc, keep other val tokens; 4plus ∪ 3)**: J>=0.5 drops 33,850 docs keeping 23,393 docs / 30.5M tokens (60%); J>=0.75 keeps 88%; J>=0.9 keeps 99%.

**Plan**: freeze J>=0.5 union drop list after mind merges -> publish clean val ids + parquet + retokenized cache (`midtrain_dedup/clean_val_v1/`) -> re-eval scaling checkpoints, refit. Driver: `scripts/analysis/nemotron_math_val_full_scan.py`; logbook `.agents/logbooks/nemotron_math_data.md`; artifacts `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/ahmed/midtrain_dedup/`.

Recommendation: fuzzy-dedup math corpora before carve-out in future runs; never trust window-level splits for templated math.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **Pointer to the CPT midtraining launch code**

For the CPT midtraining runs, the code is on branch [`midtrain_data`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/midtrain_data). A stable permalink to the current pushed state is [`89fb95bf88`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/89fb95bf8856907127cfc667129808d5888f563a).

Main entry point for the current/reproducible CPT launcher:

- [`experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py)

That launcher covers the Delphi CPT ladder from `3e18` through `1e22`. It launches **one logical cell per invocation** selected by `--base`, `--mix`, and `--lr`. The default budget is K=0.20 of the base model's pretraining token budget, i.e. the iso-FLOP CPT setting. For iso-token controls, pass `--budget-tokens N`, for example `--budget-tokens 1000000000` for 1B tokens.

Supporting code and data identity:

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/midtraining/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/midtrain_data/lib/marin/src/marin/midtraining) — the typed midtraining helpers we added/refactored: `MidtrainSpec`, CPT vs cooldown modes, budget resolution, run identity, preflight checks, manifest writing, rendered Levanter config, and Fray/Iris launch submission.
- [`experiments/midtrain_specs/__init__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/__init__.py) and [`experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections) — canonical `data:` blocks copied from the 1e21 K=0.20 reference runs so the math validation partition is byte-identical across the CPT ladder.
- [`experiments/delphi_models.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/delphi_models.py) — source of truth for Delphi base model metadata/checkpoints. This matters because the earlier issue thread corrected that the old "1e20" rows used a non-Delphi v5-isoflop base; do not choose bases by grepping GCS.
- [`experiments/exp_delphi_math_10b_midtrain.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/exp_delphi_math_10b_midtrain.py) — historical launcher for the first 10B / K=0.20 CPT sweeps. Useful for archaeology, but the newer `midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py` launcher is the one I would use for reruns/new CPT cells.

Dry-run one cell locally first:

```bash
uv run python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
  --base 3e18 --mix p33m67 --lr 0.5 --dry-run
```

Launch pattern through Iris, one top-level CPU coordinator per cell:

```bash
uv run iris --cluster=marin job run \
  --cpu 1 --memory 3GB --disk 9GB \
  --region us-east5 \
  --priority interactive \
  --no-preemptible \
  --job-name delphi-cpt-<base>-<mix>-lr<lr>-<timestamp> \
  --no-wait \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
  -e MARIN_PREFIX gs://marin-us-east5 \
  -- python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
    --base <base> --mix <mix> --lr <lr>
```

Example K=0.20 CPT cell:

```bash
uv run iris --cluster=marin job run \
  --cpu 1 --memory 3GB --disk 9GB \
  --region us-east5 \
  --priority interactive \
  --no-preemptible \
  --job-name delphi-cpt-3e18-p33m67-lr50-$(date +%s) \
  --no-wait \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
  -e MARIN_PREFIX gs://marin-us-east5 \
  -- python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
    --base 3e18 --mix p33m67 --lr 0.5
```

Example iso-token CPT cell:

```bash
uv run iris --cluster=marin job run \
  --cpu 1 --memory 3GB --disk 9GB \
  --region us-east5 \
  --priority interactive \
  --no-preemptible \
  --job-name delphi-cpt-3e18-p33m67-tok1b-lr50-$(date +%s) \
  --no-wait \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
  -e MARIN_PREFIX gs://marin-us-east5 \
  -- python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
    --base 3e18 --mix p33m67 --lr 0.5 --budget-tokens 1000000000
```

Grid selectors:

- Bases: `3e18`, `9e18`, `2e19`, `3e19`, `9e19`, `2e20`, `3e20`, `1e21`, `1e22`
- Mixes: `p33m67`, `p50m50`, `p67m33`
- LR factors: `0.33`, `0.5`, `0.67`, `0.83`

Important launch contract:

- Keep the outer Iris coordinator non-preemptible; the launcher submits the TPU child and waits for it. If the coordinator exits early, Iris can cascade-kill the child.
- Run one cell per invocation. Multi-cell sweeps should be shell/driver loops over this launcher, not one Python process submitting many children.
- The launcher rejects stale `MIDTRAIN_*`, `RUN_ID`, and `WANDB_RUN_ID` environment overrides. Run identity comes from `--base/--mix/--lr/--attempt`.
- For 1e22 or small-slice reruns, expect to need explicit TPU/memory knobs such as `--tpu`, `--ram`, `--per-device-parallelism`, and sometimes `--region`; dry-run/preflight before submitting.
- For recovery of a preempted/failed CPT run, first identify the exact old output path/run id and check permanent + temporary checkpoints. Relaunch the same logical identity/attempt with `--expected-min-step <floor>` so preflight verifies a usable checkpoint before training resumes.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **More detail: how to launch iso-token CPT runs**

If someone wants iso-token runs, use the same launcher as the K=0.20 CPT ladder, but pass `--budget-tokens N`:

```bash
python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
  --base <base> --mix <mix> --lr <lr> --budget-tokens <N>
```

What this changes:

- Default CPT budget: `BudgetPolicy.pretrain_fraction(0.20)`. This is the K=0.20 / iso-FLOP setting, so larger base models get more midtraining tokens.
- Iso-token budget: `BudgetPolicy.fixed_tokens(N)`. Every base gets the same requested total CPT token budget, with steps resolved as `round(N / (base_batch_size * 4096))`.
- Run ids change from `...-k0p20-...` to `...-tok<label>-...`, e.g. `delphi-1e22-p33m67-tok1b-lr50-a001`, so iso-token runs do not collide with K=0.20 runs.
- W&B tags include `sweep:delphi-cpt-isotoken` and `budget:tok<label>`.

Important semantic detail: `--budget-tokens` is **total training tokens through the mixture**, not necessarily math-only tokens. For a fixed mix like `p33m67`, this is fine: every scale gets the same total budget and the same expected math fraction. But if comparing different mixes, fixed total tokens does **not** fix math exposure.

Examples:

- `--mix p33m67 --budget-tokens 1000000000` means about 1B total CPT tokens, expected split about 0.33B pretrain replay + 0.67B math.
- If the desired quantity is 1B **math** tokens, convert by the math share:
  - `p33m67`: `N ~= 1B / 0.67 = 1492537313`
  - `p50m50`: `N = 2B`
  - `p67m33`: `N ~= 1B / 0.33 = 3030303030`

For the iso-token scaling controls we usually kept the mix fixed at `p33m67` and `lr=0.5`, then swept base scale and token budget.

Dry-run one cell first:

```bash
uv run python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
  --base 1e22 --mix p33m67 --lr 0.5 \
  --budget-tokens 1000000000 \
  --dry-run
```

A basic one-budget, all-base driver looks like:

```bash
BUDGET=1000000000   # 1B total CPT tokens
MIX=p33m67
LR=0.5
TS=$(date +%s)

for BASE in 3e18 9e18 2e19 3e19 9e19 2e20 3e20 1e21 1e22; do
  uv run iris --cluster=marin job run \
    --cpu 1 --memory 3GB --disk 9GB \
    --region us-east5 \
    --priority interactive \
    --no-preemptible \
    --job-name delphi-cpt-${BASE}-${MIX}-tok1b-lr50-${TS} \
    --no-wait \
    -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
    -e MARIN_PREFIX gs://marin-us-east5 \
    -- python experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py \
      --base "$BASE" --mix "$MIX" --lr "$LR" --budget-tokens "$BUDGET"
done
```

For multiple budgets, loop budgets outside the base loop. Typical budgets we used for the controls were geometric, e.g. `500000000`, `1000000000`, `2000000000`, `4000000000`, and sometimes `8000000000` for larger-budget extensions.

Useful step-count intuition for `--budget-tokens 1000000000` at `seq_len=4096`:

| base | global batch | steps for 1B total tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| `3e18` | 8 | 30518 |
| `9e18` | 16 | 15259 |
| `2e19` | 16 | 15259 |
| `3e19` | 32 | 7629 |
| `9e19` | 64 | 3815 |
| `2e20` | 64 | 3815 |
| `3e20` | 128 | 1907 |
| `1e21` | 512 | 477 |
| `1e22` | 1024 | 238 |

That asymmetry is expected. Iso-token fixes total tokens, not number of optimizer steps. Small-base runs take many more steps because their global batch is smaller; large-base runs take fewer steps because their batch is larger.

Operational notes:

- Start with `--dry-run` for every base/budget pair and inspect the planned step count, TPU, output path, and warnings.
- Keep the outer Iris coordinator non-preemptible. The nested TPU child can be preemptible; the coordinator must stay alive and wait on it.
- Use one top-level Iris job per cell. Do not make one Python invocation submit a whole grid.
- The launcher rejects stale identity env vars (`MIDTRAIN_*`, `RUN_ID`, `WANDB_RUN_ID`) so old shell state cannot silently rewrite the run id.
- For 1e22 on smaller slices, we previously needed knobs like `--tpu v5p-32 --per-device-parallelism 16 --ram 400g`; defaults are safer but may be more expensive or harder to place.
- To resume a preempted cell, reuse the same logical cell and same `--attempt`, give the outer Iris job a fresh `--job-name`, and pass `--expected-min-step <floor>`. That tells preflight to verify a permanent or temp checkpoint exists before the run resumes.

comments.author: ahmeda14960
comments.body:
🤖 **Where the pretraining + midtraining mix is defined**

The dataset mix has two layers in the codebase, and both are worth knowing about:

1. **Original declarative mix builder:** [`experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtraining_mixes.py)
2. **Frozen Delphi CPT data blocks used by the current launcher:** [`experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections), loaded by [`experiments/midtrain_specs/__init__.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/__init__.py)

The conceptual mix is built in `experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`. It composes:

- **Pretraining replay:** `nemotron_mix` from `experiments.pretraining_datasets.nemotron`
- **Midtraining math data:** `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus`, from `BUCKET_2["nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus"]`

The helper is `_replay_math_spec(...)`:

```python
def _replay_math_spec(name: str, *, pretrain_share: float, math_share: float) -> MidtrainMixSpec:
    return MidtrainMixSpec(
        name=name,
        pretrain_base=nemotron_mix,
        pretrain_share=pretrain_share,
        midtrain=(
            MidtrainComponent(
                name="nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus",
                step=_highquality_nemo_math_step,
                weight=math_share,
            ),
        ),
    )
```

Then `build_midtrain_lm_data_config(...)` turns that spec into a Levanter `LmDataConfig` by:

- scaling all `nemotron_mix.train_weights` so they sum to `pretrain_share`
- adding the math component with weight `math_share`
- merging the pretraining components and math component into one component map
- adding a held-out validation carve-out for the math component
- setting `shuffle_before_trainval_split=True`

So the registered mix specs are:

| Short name used in the Delphi CPT launcher | Original registry name | Pretraining replay | Math midtraining |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `p33m67` | `33p_67m_highquality_nemo_math` | 0.33 | 0.67 |
| `p50m50` | `50p_50m_highquality_nemo_math` | 0.50 | 0.50 |
| `p67m33` | `67p_33m_highquality_nemo_math` | 0.67 | 0.33 |

For example, `p33m67` means: take the normal Nemotron pretraining replay distribution, multiply every pretraining dataset weight by `0.33`, then add `nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus` at weight `0.67`. The resulting `train_weights` sum to 1.0.

For the current Delphi CPT launcher, we intentionally do **not** rebuild the data config dynamically from `experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`. Instead, [`experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py) calls `load_legacy_data_section(mix)` and passes that as `MidtrainSpec.data_section_override`.

Those frozen data blocks live here:

- [`experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p33m67.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p33m67.json)
- [`experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p50m50.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p50m50.json)
- [`experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p67m33.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/midtrain_data/experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/p67m33.json)

Why frozen JSON? Because we wanted the smaller-base CPT reruns, the 1e21 references, the 1e22 references, and the iso-token controls to use the **same math validation partition** byte-for-byte. The JSON files are verbatim `data:` blocks copied from the canonical 1e21 K=0.20 reference runs:

| Mix | Source run |
|---|---|
| `p33m67` | `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/delphi-1e21-p33m67-9p25b-lr0.5-efbc63` |
| `p50m50` | `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/delphi-1e21-p50m50-9p25b-lr0.5-973c46` |
| `p67m33` | `gs://marin-us-east5/checkpoints/delphi-1e21-p67m33-9p25b-lr0.5-114e49` |

All three frozen data sections share:

```text
math cache: gs://marin-us-east5/tokenized/nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus-2c5519
num_validation_sequences: {"nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus": 12500}
shuffle_before_trainval_split: true
shuffle: {io_block_size: 256, window_blocks: 512, perm_type: feistel}
```

Only `train_weights` changes across `p33m67`, `p50m50`, and `p67m33`. As a concrete example, `p33m67.json` has `"nemotron_cc_math_v1/4plus": 0.67`, and the rest of the weight mass is the scaled Nemotron pretraining replay distribution.

So the rule of thumb is:

- To understand or create a **new conceptual mix**, start with `experiments/midtraining_mixes.py`.
- To reproduce the **Delphi CPT / iso-token runs from this issue**, use `experiments/midtrain_specs/delphi_small_cpt_k020.py` with `--mix p33m67|p50m50|p67m33`; that launcher consumes the frozen JSON blocks under `experiments/midtrain_specs/data_sections/`.

# Research

The live GCS checkpoints contain 26 legacy GCP resource IDs. The `marin` checkpoint contains 25 of them; the unmatched `marin-grafana-slack-webhook` IAM member has an empty live policy, so no live resource remains solely owned by `marin-permissions`. The [#7810 operator record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7810#issuecomment-5159506589) confirms the central import completed with 716 imports, one create, and no deletions.

**Relevant code**

- [`infra/pulumi/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/pulumi/README.md) - central ownership boundary

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
The Marin vLLM fork supports schema-1 GrugMoE checkpoints exported by [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py). The EP hero exports schema 2 from [`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py); the current [`grugmoe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py) runtime and weight loader do not implement its architecture or state-dict additions.

The current [hero configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py#L86-L115) enables two shared experts, LatentMoE down/norm/up projections, distinct local and global KV-head counts, depthwise causal SConv at the K projection and attention and MLP outputs, and the interleaved fused half-RoPE convention. The export also makes the global-attention interval configurable through `global_every`; #8017 recommends an interval of 6 for future inference configurations.

Training-only changes are out of scope: QB threshold estimation, router telemetry and reductions, expert transport scheduling, capacity reporting, parameter sharding, rematerialization, and cross-entropy kernels.

Testing reference: [rav-ladder-d1536](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/rav-ladder-d1536?nw=nwuserheld) in W&B.

Done when:

- The fork reads the schema-2 configuration and applies `global_every`, `local_kv_heads`, `global_kv_heads`, `rope_fused`, `latent_dim`, `num_shared_experts`, `sconv_kernel`, and `sconv_sites` during inference.
- The loader accepts the exported latent projection/norm, indexed shared-expert, and SConv weight names.
- Prefill and token-by-token decoding match the JAX reference on a deterministic small schema-2 checkpoint, including SConv history isolation between requests.
- Existing schema-1 GrugMoE checkpoint loading and parity tests continue to pass.

Related: #6867 and #8017.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Assessment:** Actionable and well-specified, but out of scope for an automated PR: the runtime target ([`grugmoe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py)) lives in the separate `marin-community/vllm` fork, and adding the schema-2 architecture plus parity tests is a multi-module change far past the 100-line bar. Posting analysis for a human to drive.

**Research**

The fork's GrugMoE runtime and weight loader were built for schema-1 checkpoints. The EP hero exports schema 2, so config fields and state-dict tensor names the loader has never seen make the checkpoint unloadable, and several architectural features have no runtime path.

Version marker: schema-1 stamps [`GRUG_MOE_ARTIFACT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L57); the hero stamps [`= 2`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L80).

Config surface added by schema 2 ([`from_hf_config`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L290-L327), [`to_hf_config`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L329-L364)): `num_shared_experts`, `latent_dim`, `local_kv_heads`/`global_kv_heads`, `global_every`, `rope_fused`, `sconv`/`sconv_kernel`/`sconv_sites`. Hero values in [`heuristic.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py#L86-L115).

State-dict delta, schema-1 [export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L858-L903) vs schema-2 [export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1414-L1477):
- Shared experts are now indexed: `layers.{L}.shared_experts.{i}.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` (one tensor per shared expert), replacing schema-1's single joined `shared_expert.*`.
- LatentMoE tensors when `latent_dim` is set: `layers.{L}.mlp.{latent_down_proj,latent_up_proj}.weight` and `layers.{L}.mlp.latent_norm.weight`.
- SConv tensors per enabled site: `layers.{L}.self_attn.sconv_k.weight`, `layers.{L}.sconv_attn.weight`, `layers.{L}.sconv_mlp.weight`.

Runtime behavior with no schema-1 analogue:
- `global_every` layer schedule — every `global_every`-th layer and the last are full-causal, the rest sliding-window ([schedule](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1152-L1156)), with distinct KV-head counts per layer type ([attention](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L498-L529)).
- `rope_fused` interleaved fused half-RoPE convention ([apply](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L541)).
- LatentMoE compress-before-dispatch with latent RMSNorm ([MoE](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1034-L1035)).
- Depthwise causal SConv at k/attn/mlp sites ([ShortConv](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L421-L469)); decoding must carry per-request conv history and isolate it across concurrent requests.

**Proposed approach** (in the vllm fork)

1. Parse the schema-2 config in the fork's `GrugMoeConfig`, reading the fields above and branching on the version key; keep schema-1 defaults intact.
2. Extend the weight loader to accept indexed `shared_experts.{i}`, the latent projections/norm, and the SConv weights; keep the schema-1 single-`shared_expert` path.
3. Implement runtime: per-layer local/global sliding-vs-full schedule via `global_every`, `rope_fused` RoPE, LatentMoE compress/expand, N summed shared experts, and SConv with per-sequence causal state threaded through the paged-attention decode loop (the isolation requirement).
4. Parity test against the JAX reference on a small deterministic schema-2 checkpoint: prefill and token-by-token decode, plus a multi-request case that proves SConv history does not leak between sequences. Keep the existing schema-1 loading/parity tests green.

Reference exporter to mirror exactly: [`grugmoe_inference_state_dict`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py#L1414-L1477). Related: #6867, #8017 (recommends `global_every=6` for inference). Training-only concerns (QB estimation, router telemetry, transport scheduling, sharding, remat, CE kernels) stay out of scope.

🤖

# Research

The IaC workflow previews five production stacks for pull-request updates but has no merged-PR event or deployment follow-up. Its artifacts already expose per-stack change/error metadata, and the preview identity can read and decrypt state without writing it.

# Proposed Fix

Extend the preview workflow with a merged-PR mode that checks the PR's merge commit after 30 minutes, keeping later merges out of that PR's result. If any stack still reports changes or an error, upsert a reminder mentioning the merger and dispatch the same workflow for two more checks after 60 and 120 minutes; retain the existing parallel stack previews and read-only identity.

## Description
Add a selectable TPU paged-attention backend for Levanter inference so Qwen3-style paged decode can use the pinned `tpu-inference` kernels on TPU while keeping reference and JAX RPA paths available for diagnostics and tests.

This tracks the implementation in #6099. The change should keep the model decode path native to Levanter, pass the paged-attention policy through inference decode, and preserve CPU-safe tests and fallback behavior.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
## Description
Generalize the paged-attention execution config introduced in #6099 from `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` to a backend-neutral `PagedAttentionConfig` draccus choice family.

The current config combines backend selection with TPU-specific tuning fields. That is already awkward for `tpu-inference` versus JAX RPA, and it will get worse once a GPU implementation lands. Keep the policy passed through decode, but make the config type generic and dispatch by concrete choice type rather than a TPU-only enum.

Suggested choices: `auto`, `reference`, `tpu-inference`, `jax-rpa`, and later a GPU backend choice.

### Definition of Done
- `decode` and attention call sites accept `PagedAttentionConfig`, not `TpuPagedAttentionConfig`.
- TPU-specific tunables live only on TPU-specific choice dataclasses.
- `paged_attention_with_kv_update` dispatches by config choice type.
- Existing TPU paged-attention tests cover the renamed/generic config surface.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue and AGENTS / fix-issue / author-pr skills
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (PR #6099, related issues)
- [x] Inspect `TpuPagedAttentionConfig`, dispatch, and call sites on the #6099 branch
- [x] Decide on PR vs analysis: posting analysis (depends on #6099; design change spans 5+ files)

**Research**

The code this issue refers to lives only on the open draft [PR #6099](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6099) (`codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention`); nothing matching `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` / `paged_attention_with_kv_update` is on `main` yet. The current `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` mixes three concerns: backend selection (generic), dispatch policy (`allow_autotune`, `fail_on_reference_fallback` — generic), and backend-specific tunables (`tpu_inference_out_dtype`, `preserve_attention_output_dtype` for tpu-inference; `num_kv_pages_per_block`, `num_queries_per_block`, `vmem_limit_bytes` for JAX RPA). Dispatch is a string-enum if/elif chain in `_run_backend`, so adding a GPU backend later means widening every model signature and growing the enum/branch list.

Relevant code (PR #6099 branch):
- [`tpu_kernels.py#L22-L41`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/tpu_kernels.py#L22-L41) — `TpuPagedAttentionBackend` enum + `TpuPagedAttentionConfig` dataclass.
- [`tpu_kernels.py#L301-L396`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/tpu_kernels.py#L301-L396) — `_run_backend` / `paged_attention_with_kv_update` enum dispatch and fallback chain.
- [`attention.py#L1777`, `#L1961`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L1777) — call sites in `PagedKvCacheAttention.decode` variants.
- [`llama.py#L357`, `#L431`, `#L641`, `#L685`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/llama.py#L357) and [`apertus.py#L301`, `#L363`, `#L484`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/apertus.py#L301) — model decode signatures.
- [`test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/tests/inference/test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py), [`test_qwen3.py#L18`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/levanter-tpu-paged-attention/lib/levanter/tests/test_qwen3.py#L18) — tests that construct the config.

**Proposed Approach (for review before implementing)**

Treat this as a design change to land **after** #6099 merges; opening a parallel PR off the draft branch would conflict. Suggested shape:

1. New module `lib/levanter/src/levanter/inference/paged_attention_config.py`:
   - Abstract base `PagedAttentionConfig` registered with draccus as a choice family.
   - Generic policy fields on the base: `fail_on_reference_fallback: bool`, plus multi-backend ordering handled via a wrapper like `AutoPagedAttentionConfig(candidates=...)` rather than a magic `AUTO` enum value.
   - Concrete choices: `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig`, `JaxRpaPagedAttentionConfig` (holds `num_kv_pages_per_block`, `num_queries_per_block`, `vmem_limit_bytes`), `TpuInferencePagedAttentionConfig` (holds `out_dtype`, `preserve_attention_output_dtype`, `vmem_limit_bytes`), and later `GpuPagedAttentionConfig`.
   - Each choice exposes a `run(q, new_k, new_v, kv_cache, batch_info, *, sm_scale, soft_cap) -> tuple[NamedArray, KvPageCache]` method; `paged_attention_with_kv_update` becomes a thin entry point that walks the candidate list, catches `UnsupportedPagedAttentionBackend`, and emits a fallback warning. No `if/elif backend == ...` chain remains.

2. Rename the `tpu_paged_attention` parameter on `PagedKvCacheAttention.decode`, `LlamaDecoderLayer.decode`, `LlamaTransformer.decode`, `LlamaLMHeadModel.decode`, and the Apertus equivalents to `paged_attention: PagedAttentionConfig`. Default to `AutoPagedAttentionConfig()`.

3. Keep `TpuPagedAttentionShape` and platform/shape gating helpers, but move them into the TPU-specific choice classes (they call `tpu_paged_attention_supports_shape` internally). No backward-compat shim per AGENTS.md "NO BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY".

4. Update `test_tpu_paged_attention_backends.py` and `test_qwen3.py` to construct concrete choices (`JaxRpaPagedAttentionConfig()`, `TpuInferencePagedAttentionConfig()`, `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig()`) and parameterize on those directly instead of the string enum.

5. Estimated diff: ~400-600 lines across `tpu_kernels.py` (split into `paged_attention_config.py` + `tpu_pallas_backend.py`), `tpu_inference_adapter.py` (no signature change), `attention.py`, `llama.py`, `apertus.py`, two test files. Above the <100 LOC PR threshold, hence this design comment instead of a direct PR.

**Open questions for the issue author**

- Should the choice family base live in `levanter.inference` (next to backends) or in `levanter.layers.attention` (next to the call sites)?
- Is `AutoPagedAttentionConfig(candidates=[...])` the preferred way to express the current `AUTO` policy, or do you want a top-level `auto` choice that internally re-resolves to a platform-derived default each call?
- Confirm the `fail_on_reference_fallback` semantics belong on the base config rather than only on `ReferencePagedAttentionConfig` — keeping it on the base preserves today's "I picked tpu-inference and refuse to silently fall back to reference" behaviour.

Will wait for confirmation on #6099 merging and the questions above before opening a PR.
